terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where try.js sends requests with and without tokens, and one to an app whose store is broken on purpose.

tasks.title: Lock the write routes
tasks.description:
Implement `requireStaff(req, res, tokens)` in `src/auth.js`, then call it at the very start of `createBoat`, `updateBoat` and `deleteBoat` in `src/app.js`. `tokens` is a `Map` from token to role, passed to every handler.

- no `authorization` header, a header that is not `Bearer <token>`, or a token not in the map: set the header `www-authenticate: Bearer` on `res` and throw `new HttpError(401, 'unauthorized', message)`
- a known token whose role is not `'staff'`: throw `new HttpError(403, 'forbidden', message)`
- otherwise return the role

The word `Bearer` may arrive in any case. `GET` routes stay open. The check starts your app with its own tokens and tries every write route with no token, a wrong token, a viewer token and a staff token.
nextSteps: Read `req.headers.authorization` and pull the token out of it.
Look the token up in the map and decide between 401, 403 and success.
Call `requireStaff` first thing in the three write handlers.
Run `node try.js` and read the answers to the three POST requests.
hints: 401 means we do not know who you are. 403 means we know, and the answer is still no.
A regular expression with the `i` flag can match the scheme in any case and capture the token after it.
Check the token before `readJson`, otherwise a client with no token learns about JSON errors first. `/^Bearer +(\S+)$/i` captures the token in group 1.

tasks.title: One place for errors
tasks.description:
Implement `handleError(err, req, res, log)` in `src/errors.js`, then make the `catch` in `createApp` call it with the `log` from the options.

- an `HttpError` answers its `status` with `{ error: { code, message, details }, requestId }`
- any other error is a bug: call `log(...)` with the error, and answer `500` with `{ error: { code: 'internal_error', message }, requestId }`, where the message is a fixed sentence that says nothing about the error
- `requestId` is `res.getHeader('x-request-id')`
- if `res.headersSent` is already true, call `res.destroy()` instead of answering

Right now a crash sends its own message to the client. The check throws an error that contains a password and a server address, and looks for them in the response.
nextSteps: Run `node try.js` and read the last answer. That message should never reach a client.
Write the HttpError branch, then the branch for everything else.
Log the real error in the second branch.
Replace the body of the catch in `createApp` with one call.
hints: An error message is written for developers. It can hold file paths, hostnames, queries and secrets.
The client needs to know that it failed and how to report it. The team needs the details. Each gets its own channel.
Use `err instanceof HttpError` to choose the branch, `log('request', requestId, 'failed:', err)` for the details, and a constant message in the 500 body.

tasks.title: A request id on every response
tasks.description:
Implement `requestIdFor(req)` in `src/requestId.js`, then set `res.setHeader('x-request-id', requestIdFor(req))` as the first thing `createApp`'s request handler does.

- if the request has an `x-request-id` header of 1 to 64 characters, all letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`, return it
- otherwise return a new id from `randomUUID()`

Every response then carries the id, including 404s and errors, and `handleError` puts the same value in error bodies as `requestId`. The check compares headers across several requests and against the body of two error answers.
nextSteps: Read the incoming header and test it against the allowed pattern.
Return it, or a new UUID.
Set the header in `createApp` before `handleRequest` runs.
Run `node try.js` and match the ids in headers and bodies.
hints: An id that comes from the client is input like any other. It will end up in your logs, so only accept a safe shape.
Setting the header before routing means every answer has it, even ones you did not think about.
`/^[\w.-]{1,64}$/` matches the allowed shape. `req.headers['x-request-id']` is a string or undefined.
